category_title: Students with learning disabilities who use abbreviations and pre-quizzes to prioritize lecture content
minimal_context: Noah is attempting to take notes on a blank piece of paper while watching a 15-minute video lecture on Electro-Plasma Rockets.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to watch this 15-minute video lecture on Electro-Plasma Rockets. Please take notes on the important points using your notebook paper.

STUDENT: He's talking really fast. I'm trying to write these bigger sentences but it takes too much time.

TUTOR: Just keep listening and write down what you hear.

STUDENT: I don't know what the most important part of the topic is. I'm missing the clues about what I'm supposed to be paying attention to.

TUTOR: Try your best to catch up and focus on the main ideas.

STUDENT: I can't do it. I'm writing too slow to understand the information from the lecture, and I have zero critical points written down so far.

options.A: Build personal relationships outside of the classroom context by visiting with the student and their family in their home.
options.B: Have the student complete reflective journal entries in which they are encouraged to write or draw freely about the video lecture.
options.C: Gather data on the student's appropriate note-taking behavior and disruptive behavior during the video lecture using a scatter plot.
options.D: Provide explicit training including descriptions, modeling, guided practice with a video lecture, and acclimation to the lecture pace.
